title: curie scenario --json
description: The agent-facing payload of `curie scenario <MANIFEST> --json`: the ticket, the artifact that was run, and one entry per selected tier carrying its runtime-identity readings, its graded probes and its verified teardown. The SAME shape is emitted on the red path, where `error` and `fix` are non-null.

ticket.description: The ticket the scenario answers, verbatim from the manifest.

bundle_path.description: The resolved absolute path of the bundle that was packaged.

source_commit.description: The bundle tree's commit. Always present; null outside a git tree, never fabricated.

artifact_digest.description: sha256 of the tar.gz the run packed once and booted on, computed exactly the way `apps/api` computes it on deploy.

model_mode.description: The model the manifest declares, asserted against the live container before any probe runs.

error.description: The run's diagnosis, or null. Always present so an agent consumer can read it unconditionally.

fix.description: The actionable remedy for `error`, or null.

tiers.description: One entry per selected tier, accumulated in order: a later failure never erases an earlier tier's result.

verdict.description: `plumbing_ok` is a third state, not a shade of pass: the turns completed on the fake model and were therefore never graded (ADR-0055).

identity_verified.description: Whether the booted container was proved to be running the artifact this run packed. False fails closed: no probe runs against an unverified container.

mounted_snapshot_dir.description: The source path the Docker DAEMON reports bound at /plugin, not our own record. Null when the container reports no such mount, which is a mismatch rather than a pass.

container_fake_model.description: Whether the live container carries CURIE_FAKE_MODEL, read back from the daemon. Null when the read failed.

probes.description: One row per probe, in manifest order. Empty when identity verification aborted the tier before any turn was sent.

error.description: This tier's diagnosis. A teardown failure never overwrites it; that one is carried in `teardown.error`.

kind.description: A negative probe is the falsifiability control: it passes only when its grader does NOT match.

acceptance_criteria.description: The ticket criteria this probe answers, so every row is bound to what it proves.

outcome.description: The probe's verdict, after the positive/negative inversion. Reuses the frozen eval-case vocabulary.

passed.description: Tri-state view of `outcome`: true for pass, false for fail, null for plumbing_ok. A non-graded row claims neither verdict.

grader_matched.description: The RAW grader result, BEFORE the kind inversion, so a red control is diagnosable without a re-run. Null when nothing was graded.

reply.description: The graded answer text. `<no reply text>` when the turn produced none.

attempted.description: Teardown is unconditional: a tier that booted a container owns one whatever went wrong afterwards.

container_removed.description: Asserted against the daemon after the removal, never assumed from a `docker rm` that exited 0. A stranded container turns the run red.

state_cleared.description: Asserted on the filesystem: the bundle's runner record is gone.

snapshot_released.description: Asserted on the filesystem: the snapshot directory this run packed is gone.

error.description: The teardown's own diagnosis, carried separately so it never overwrites the reason the tier was already red.
